topic: How do orbital altitude and inclination choices in GNSS constellations balance global coverage versus signal power margins?
consensus_response: The trade-off between orbital altitude and inclination affects signal propagation, influencing global coverage and signal power margins. Higher altitudes reduce free-space losses but increase latency, while lower altitudes improve global coverage by increasing satellite visibility but compromise signal power due to increased free-space losses. Geometry optimization techniques can balance these trade-offs by adjusting satellite positions and orientations. The choice of altitude and inclination affects the constellation's capacity, interference patterns, and overall performance.
